Gains over the primary retrievers are consistent on ViDoRe 2 and 3. Colnomic improves from 60.3 to 63.1 NDCG@5 on ViDoRe 2 and from 55.7 to 57.4 on ViDoRe 3, with the latter using transferred hyperparameters. The reported latency comparison with Llama-Nemo also suggests a useful practical tradeoff.
weaknesses: The central comparison does not isolate the benefit of query refinement. Appendix C normalizes fusion scores within each retriever's top-K list and assigns zero to documents outside that list, whereas GQR scores every candidate in the union using both retrievers. A fusion baseline using the same fully rescored candidate pool is necessary to distinguish representation optimization from additional scoring information.

The advantage over the strongest fusion baseline is small and lacks uncertainty analysis. On ViDoRe 2, GQR achieves 62.3 versus 62.1 NDCG@5 and 58.6 versus 58.5 Recall@5. On ViDoRe 3, relative improvements are 2.89% versus 2.66%. Standard deviations across model pairs do not establish the reliability of these differences; paired confidence intervals and individual model-pair comparisons are needed.

Methodological novelty is limited relative to the acknowledged test-time query optimization literature. The main changes are using a complementary bi-encoder and a moving consensus target. Table 18 shows that direct teacher KL and Jensen-Shannon objectives frequently match or outperform the proposed consensus objective, leaving its distinctive benefit insufficiently established.

The efficiency evidence does not establish GQR's claimed Pareto advantage over competitive hybrid retrieval. The latency and storage plots omit tuned score fusion using the same model pairs, which would retain the same indexes while avoiding iterative optimization. The headline memory reduction concerns document representations rather than total deployment memory, and the unspecified retrieval backend and absence of corpus-size scaling experiments limit broader scalability claims.

The tuning protocol disadvantages fusion when the complementary retriever is unhelpful: weights are restricted to 0.1–0.9, excluding the option to retain the primary retriever alone. GQR can approximate that option through very small updates. This particularly weakens the ViDoRe 1 robustness comparison.

Reproducibility and reporting need improvement. The manuscript announces released code without providing a link and omits exact split identifiers and important indexing/timing details. There are also numerical inconsistencies: Table 19 reports 61.17 for Jina-vision plus Qwen3 with a gain of 2.6, whereas Table 1 reports 59.8 against a 57.2 baseline. These issues, together with the unresolved baseline comparison, leave insufficient evidence for acceptance.
